scope: model/flux.py (new), model/composite.py, model/api.py, evaluation/test_model.py, evaluation/test_unit_flux.py -- no checkpoint changed

summary.what: default flux calibration switched from a finite-grid trapezoid integral with a hard-capped shift ('legacy') to a Gauss-Legendre quadrature (geometric panels near the exact body support boundary, refined until mass/inverse-moment agree to 2e-6) enforcing <1/mu>=1 exactly ('unit', new default)
summary.why: more accurate normalization/flux integral than the old finite-range trapezoid grid; removes the historical GRID_HI=ln(400) truncation

first_version_regression_and_fix.first_version: no cap on the unit-flux shift -- flux.unit_flux_context's own docstring said so explicitly

regression_found.method: 973-context untouched test-set qualification (experiments/unit_flux_implementation_2026-09-07/qualify.py), comparing kl_legacy vs kl_unit per context

by_z_band.z_0_to_8: kl_unit ~= kl_legacy (identical to 3-4 decimals) across 877/973 contexts

regression_found.root_cause: correlation(|shift|, kl_unit) = 0.974 across all 973 contexts, vs correlation(z, kl_unit) = 0.47 -- shift MAGNITUDE is the real driver, not z per se (confirmed: at least one z=6.79 context with a large shift shows the same blowup). Every one of the worst-affected contexts had the LEGACY shift already saturated at its own -0.05 cap, i.e. this is direct evidence the historical cap was a genuine, load-bearing trust region, not conservative slack to relax.

first_version_regression_and_fix.fix: composite.py's context() now clips the unit-flux shift to the SAME FLUX_DELTA_MAX=0.05 the legacy path already used, identically applied (float(np.clip(delta, -FLUX_DELTA_MAX, FLUX_DELTA_MAX))). The more accurate Gauss-Legendre quadrature itself is unchanged and kept for every context -- only the size of the correction it's allowed to apply is now bounded. flux.unit_flux_context itself is left uncapped and documented as such, so it remains a general-purpose 'what would exact unit flux require here' utility independent of this policy choice.
first_version_regression_and_fix.cap_calibration_evidence: binned by |shift|: (0,0.05] -> 865/973 contexts, kl_unit==kl_legacy to 4 decimals; (0.05,0.1] -> kl_unit already 2.5x kl_legacy's own median in that bin; degradation grows monotonically past that point. The pre-existing 0.05 value (unchanged from the legacy path, not re-tuned) is already well-calibrated -- 89% of the test set never reaches it.

post_fix_verification.spot_check: 5 worst-affected contexts from the uncapped run (production_data:{80,376,596,790,949}, z in [10.2,11.6]) re-checked directly: all now have delta clipped to exactly -0.0500 and KL_unit == KL_legacy to 4 decimals
post_fix_verification.pytest: 24/24 pass (production_model/evaluation), including a new test_extreme_context_is_capped_not_exact replacing the original test's now-incorrect assumption that z=10.43 achieves exact unit flux

not_claimed: the 108 capped contexts do NOT have exact unit flux -- this is deliberate, not a residual bug
this does not address the pre-existing (unrelated) monotonicity violations documented in PROVENANCE.md's 2026-09-07 tail-anchor-correction section, found independently the same day
